previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ , a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a chronic Foley catheter, was admitted for evaluation of gross hematuria following a recent traumatic catheter change. He had no fever, pain, or signs of systemic infection. Labs showed bacteriuria and pyuria, but clinical assessment concluded this represented asymptomatic colonization rather than active urinary tract infection. The hematuria was attributed to urethral trauma during catheter replacement and resolved without intervention. His chronic unintentional weight loss was evaluated with normal thyroid, inflammatory, metabolic, and imaging studies; outpatient cancer screening was recommended. He remained neurologically stable, continued on home medications including fluoxetine and oxybutynin, and was discharged home after 3 days with instructions to monitor for symptoms and follow up with primary care and specialists.
problems: Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, in remission

Brief Hospital Course:
# Weakness: Suspected likely infection due to leukocytosis and 
symptoms typical of prior UTIs. UTI most likely potentiated by 
neurogenic bladder and recently stopping methenamine. UA only 
with WBC 18, but in past UA's have had varying amount of WBC in 
urine with positive cultures. CXR without evidence of pneumonia. 
He was started on meropenum and vancomycin for broad coverage  
given history of ESBL and enterococcus  and immunosuppression 
with recent solumedrol infusion. His foley was also replaced 
with a new one. He also received a 2L NS bolus as he appeared 
dehydrated. Patient's weakness greatly improved with antibiotics 
and he stated he was at baseline. Urine culture showed 
pseudomonas, e.coli, and entercocci. Following culture results, 
patient was discharge with prescriptions for Cipro and Augmentin 
based on sensitivities.  He was also given a Rx for methenamine 
for UTI ppx.

injections with progressive gait instability, now uses wheel 
chair. Remained stable during admission and he will continue 
methylprednisolone as outpt. Patient already has home aid and 
supports established
